svg.text: AI-SOC DATA FLOW
One alert, end to end — from an external detection tool to a closed case
Version 2.7.1 — Summer 2026
PHASE A — SYNCHRONOUS INTAKE · NOTHING MAY BE LOST
A Splunk saved search fires · its alert action POSTs the raw result
POST /detections?adapter=splunk — POST /splunk-alert is a thin compatibility alias for the same thing
AI-SOC does not poll, holds no index and never receives raw logs. Detection belongs to the external tool.
1 · Authentication gate — scope detections:write
Checked before the body is read. The ingest role holds this one scope and nothing else.
This is the route that, with autopilot enabled, ends in a dispatched network action.
2 · Adapter — the only place in the system where a vendor is named
Splunk's field names become the Detection Intake contract: source tool · rule identity · detected_at converted to UTC ·
severity normalised from the vendor's own scale beside the verbatim value · the ATT&CK the tool itself asserted · entities · raw payload
Placeholders (unknown · - · n/a) are stripped here: correlating on one would join every unrelated detection in the window into one situation.
3 · Source registry and metrics
Last seen, adapter version, health and trust weight for that tool — recorded before anything downstream can fail.
4 · Cross-tool correlation → SECURITY SITUATION
Joins on a shared strong entity — user · host · address · file hash · URL — inside the correlation window. Never on the text of a rule name.
Deterministic risk score with its factors kept beside it: highest severity · +12 per corroborating tool · volume · lateral shape · × source trust.
Two situations a later detection ties together are merged. One whose decision has left PENDING stops absorbing, and the next opens its own.
5 · The split — parse, store and correlate are synchronous; the model call is a job
Everything above this line is fast and must never be lost. Below it is the slow, failable half — and the only part worth retrying.
Inline is the default, so a caller still carries its own decision back in the response.
Back-pressure sheds latency, never data.
PHASE B — THE ANALYSIS JOB · SLOW, FAILABLE, RETRYABLE
6 · The worker reloads the situation by id, not the object it was handed
Between the job being written and the job being run the situation may have grown — the analysis must be of the situation as it is.
7 · Threat-intelligence enrichment — a client, never a platform
Four buckets: malicious · suspicious · not_found (asked, no record) · skipped (never asked, with a reason). UNKNOWN is not BENIGN.
Private, loopback and reserved addresses are never sent out. A feed that times out reports degraded — never empty-and-therefore-clean.
8 · Precedent retrieval — what this SOC decided the last time it saw this shape
Weighted similarity over past settled decisions: techniques 30 · narrative 20 · sources 15 · entities 15 · entity shape 10 · severity 10.
A failure here costs the analyst context, not the verdict — it logs and returns nothing.
9 · Prompt assembly
The situation document (N detections from M tools · the entity graph · the time span · the tools' own techniques) · the intel report · precedents to cite
10 · Local inference
Enforced JSON output · the reasoning preamble suppressed · a token budget wide enough for the whole object · low temperature.
The model reasons over the situation, not over one alert. A model-free mode runs this entire path with no inference at all.
11 · Parse and normalise — where the model is held to account
A response that will not parse raises. It never falls back to the reply envelope, which would parse cleanly and silently default every field.
The tool's asserted technique outranks the model's. Every ID is checked against the catalogue: verified · unlisted · unknown · malformed.
A precedent id the model invented is dropped from the reasoning — and kept, because a model that invents case ids is a fact worth having.
12 · Persist the analysed record
A new situation creates one. A situation that has grown is re-analysed in place and its proposal re-derived over the enlarged picture.
13 · Tier-2 verdict — CONTAIN · ESCALATE · INVESTIGATE · MONITOR · IGNORE
Validation is deliberately asymmetric: a verdict outside the vocabulary discards the whole proposal; a missing field falls back on its own.
Each action is classified READ · LOW_WRITE · HIGH_WRITE · DESTRUCTIVE and its target parsed. An unmodelled verb is HIGH_WRITE, never READ.
A refused action keeps its row, its position in the plan and its reason, and the analyst sees it before approving. Status: PENDING.
14 · A case is opened the moment the situation is analysed
Not when an analyst first opens it — a case created on first view cannot answer “what came in overnight and who has it”.
15 · Autopilot gate — off by default; Stage 2 means a human confirms
All four gates must hold and the plan is all-or-nothing. Any refusal leaves the decision PENDING for a person.
The machine's own approvals are marked as such, so autopilot can never become its own precedent.
PHASE C — HUMAN CONFIRMATION AND DISPATCH
16 · The analyst — Approve · Reject · Edit
The dashboard shows the verdict, the rationale, the intel report, the cited precedents, and the plan with its blocked actions already marked.
An edit writes the correction before the decision row is overwritten: original verdict and its source, corrected verdict, actions added and removed.
Approve and Reject record that the machine was wrong. Only an edit records what right looks like.
17 · Approved — a whitelist, not a blacklist
Only a PENDING decision may be approved. Actions move to QUEUED, execution runs in the background and the API returns at once.
18 · Delivery, action by action
Policy is re-checked at dispatch. Routing is by action class, not by deployment — block-ip to the firewall, isolate to the EDR, the rest to SOAR.
Every action carries an idempotency key stable across retries. Only transport failures are retried: a refusal is an answer, delivered once.
A success code is not delivery — a connector that cannot observe success never reports DONE.
19 · Settle
Every action delivered → the alert is mitigated and the decision reads DONE. Any failure → FAILED.
Rendering a simulation as a completed containment is the most dangerous thing this system could get wrong.
PHASE D — THE LOOP CLOSES
20 · Case sync with the system of record
AI-SOC owns severity, verdict and evidence; the ticketing system owns owner, state and closure. An inbound message can never cause an action.
21 · Outcome, inside the feedback window
TRUE_POSITIVE · FALSE_POSITIVE · REOPENED. The window exists because the judgement perishes: three days is answerable, three months is not.
Precision is reported per detection source as well as per decision source — a bad upstream rule and a bad model produce the same symptom.
THE DECISION STORE
detections
contract 1 — the vendor payload verbatim
situations
contract 2 — members · entity graph ·
risk score with its factors
analysis_jobs
what still owes a decision · attempts ·
the dead letters
read — the precedent corpus
past settled decisions, and whether
each of them turned out to be right
security_events
the analysed record + containment steps
tier2_decisions
with provenance: llm · rules · human —
the column that makes a silent model
failure detectable at all
cases · case_events
append-only, every entry stamped
human · system · sync
decision_corrections
the label corpus — what a human
changed, and what had been proposed
alert_soar_actions
receipts · risk class · policy verdict ·
idempotency key · attempts
decision_outcomes
attributed to the detection source
Retention drops copies of documents
the upstream tool still holds. It never
touches a decision, a correction, an
outcome or a receipt — those exist in
exactly one place, and nothing
upstream can reproduce them.
— this is where the loop closes
401 — unauthenticated
Refused before the body is even parsed.
422 · 400 — the payload is not a detection
Unreadable, or missing a required key. One carrying
neither a rule nor an entity is refused, not ingested.
202 — stored and correlated, decision queued
When the deployment asked for it, the backlog is past the
high-water mark, or this situation is already being analysed.
502 — the model is down
The detection and situation are stored, and a retry is scheduled.
EXTERNAL — THREAT INTELLIGENCE
An on-prem MISP · a local indicator file · none
“none” is honest rather than empty: nothing then reads as verified.
The corpus is decisions, not documents
Entity identity is deliberately outweighed by technique and
shape: precedent is about the shape of an intrusion, not
about the same host offending twice.
ON-PREM INFERENCE
A local model server. No cloud inference, ever.
The confidence it reports is uncalibrated — display and ordering only.
The three failures that look like success
· a truncated response a tolerant parser “rescues”
· a thinking model that returns an empty string
· the reply envelope parsed as if it were the answer
When the proposal is unusable
The severity rule decides instead and the row is stamped
decision_source = rules, so a later review can find every
decision a degraded or absent model produced.
The four gates
1 · the verdict is auto-executable 2 · confidence clears a floor
3 · every action passes the risk policy 4 · precedent supports it
Gates 3 and 4 are the ones that protect the network.
An edit can be refused
422 — the edited plan contains an action that could never
dispatch; storing it would show a plan that silently blocks.
409 — already approved: the row is now the record of what was sent.
EXTERNAL — EXECUTION
SOAR · EDR · firewall · identity provider
A refused action is BLOCKED before a packet leaves, and keeps its
row, its position in the plan and the reason it was refused.
A dry run is SIMULATED, never DONE
Nothing was sent, the alert is not mitigated and the decision
never reads DONE. Start every deployment here.
EXTERNAL — SYSTEM OF RECORD
TheHive · Jira · ServiceNow · a directory drop
Legend:
the main path
external tool — out of scope
refused
held, degraded or deferred — never lost
dashed = an external dependency or a store access
